title: Git & GitHub
tagline: Make Git's model visible, then use it like a professional team does.
description: Most people learn Git as a list of spells: type these words, hope nothing breaks, delete the folder when it does. This course takes the other route. You learn what a commit, a branch and HEAD actually are, so every command becomes a predictable move on a graph you can draw, and a scary message becomes a situation you can read.

You practise on one real thing: your own portfolio site. It starts as a folder with git init, picks up branches, a merge conflict and a GitHub remote, and finishes as a protected main branch where every change arrives through a pull request that GitHub Actions has checked. Along the way you learn to undo almost anything safely.
audience: Career switchers and junior developers who use Git a little, fear it a lot, and want to work confidently on a team.
prerequisites: Comfort with a terminal (cd, ls, opening files) and a free GitHub account; no Git experience needed.
learnItems: Explain commits, branches and HEAD as a graph you can draw
Stage and commit deliberately, and read history with log, diff and show
Merge, rebase and resolve conflicts without panic
Push, pull and review code through GitHub pull requests
Undo mistakes safely with restore, revert, reset and the reflog
Ship a CI-checked, protected main branch with Actions and rulesets
